title: Paper Courier
premise: A cartoon delivery courier speeds down a city road, weaving around descending barriers to keep the route alive and rack up package deliveries.
interaction_model: Single-screen touch/pointer steering game where the player drags horizontally to guide the courier vehicle while everything rushes downward.
objective: Survive as long as possible, avoid crashing into road barriers, and build the highest delivery score through survival and successful obstacle passes.
progression: The run starts manageable, then the rush multiplier steadily increases over time, making the road feel faster, obstacle spawning denser, and scoring more lucrative until a crash ends the session.
theme: Arcade paper-delivery rush in a bright cartoon city streetscape.
mood: Playful, upbeat, hectic, colorful, and restart-friendly.
likely_audience: Casual mobile arcade players, endless runner fans, and younger audiences who enjoy simple one-touch score-chasing games.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an endless dodge-survival arcade game built around horizontal courier steering.
Moderate confidence that the fiction is newspaper/package delivery rather than generic courier driving, based on the title, envelope iconography, and UI text.
Moderate confidence on genre labeling between endless runner and lane runner because the game is free horizontal movement on a single-screen road rather than discrete lanes.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a mobile-friendly HTML5 arcade game called Paper Courier where the player controls a small cartoon courier car with an envelope emblem on a stylized city road and survives as long as possible by dragging left and right to dodge descending traffic-cone barriers. Present the action on a full-screen canvas with a bright sky gradient, a tapered road, roadside grass, a distant skyline, and punchy comic-book UI panels. Use a simple endless-run loop: the courier stays near the bottom of the screen, obstacles spawn from the top and move downward, score rises continuously over time and also increases when barriers are successfully passed, and a visible rush multiplier gradually climbs to make movement and spawning faster. Include responsive touch/pointer steering with eased horizontal movement, a deliveries counter, a rush-speed HUD, short success and crash feedback, energetic audio cues, light haptics on good passes if available, paper-scrap particle explosions on collision, and an immediate game-over overlay with the final package count plus a restart button. Keep the tone colorful, playful, and fast, emphasizing short repeatable runs, escalating pressure, and clean mobile presentation.
